expected_concepts: Alterbiography (Calleja's signature term — emergent narrative generated by individual player as she takes action in game)
Scripted narrative (pre-scripted story events written into the game)
Narratology-vs-ludology debate (Calleja's stance: takes up Juul-vs-Aarseth without endorsing either pole)
Story-vs-game tension (story-time vs discourse-time collapse in games per Juul 2001)
Speech-act approach to narrative (Ryan 2006 — narrative as retelling, requires narrator)
Story / discourse / narrating distinction (Genette Saussurian terms)
Embedded vs emergent narrative (Salen + Zimmerman 2003)
Narrative descriptors / narrative operators (Pearce 2004 — experiential, performative, augmentary, descriptive, metastory, story system)
Environmental storytelling / evocative spaces (Jenkins 2004)
Push narrative (designer-imposed delivery via cut scenes, quick-time events)
Pull narrative (player-elicited narrative — Ken Levine on Bioshock audio diaries)
Scripted narrative delivery channels (cut scenes, quick-time events, objects in world, dialog, verbal text)
Structures of progression (linear / branching / open-with-main-line / open-with-side-quests-only)
Alterbiography of self (first-person focalization)
Alterbiography of entity (third-person focalization)
Alterbiography of environment (general / managerial focalization)
Synthesis (player's interpretive combination of rules + representation + imagination — Sartre/Iser-derived)
Ergodic media and narrative (Aarseth — narrative anchored in mechanical/coded structures, not surface signs)
Narrative affordances (generic, NOT Gibson-cited — narrative-generating properties of interaction)
Cognitive / mental construct approach to narrative (Ryan 2006)
Story-driven games vs system-driven games
Narrative experience vs general thoughts about game (Calleja's critique of Salen + Zimmerman's poker example)
Distinction between scripted-narrative-time and player-action-time

expected_interlocutors.name: Marie-Laure Ryan
expected_interlocutors.role: Tier-A interlocutor — supplies the 'speech-act approach to narrative' framing; the 'narrative as cognitive/mental construct' alternative; corrective to Eskelinen + Juul that games merely tell stories DIFFERENTLY, not non-narratively. Most-cited theorist in the chapter.

expected_interlocutors.name: Jesper Juul
expected_interlocutors.role: Tier-A foil — supplies the 'cannot have interactivity and narration at the same time' claim that Calleja directly critiques by introducing the scripted-narrative/alterbiography distinction. Juul's story-time = discourse-time = reading/viewing-time collapse argument is Calleja's primary launch point.

expected_interlocutors.name: Espen Aarseth
expected_interlocutors.work: Cybertext (1997); Quest Games as Post-Narrative Discourse (2004)
expected_interlocutors.role: Tier-A — invoked twice, once supporting the importance of ergodic mechanical structures (echoing Salen+Zimmerman's emergent narrative), once as one of the 'are games narratives?' question-framers. Ergodic-media argument central.

expected_interlocutors.name: Markku Eskelinen

expected_burke_pentad_candidate: Act + Purpose (anticipatory projection per plan §4.1 — provenance: anticipatory-projection). Narrative involvement structurally aligns with Burke's Act (what was done) plus Purpose (toward what end), because scripted narrative supplies a teleological structure (Purpose) while alterbiography is the running record of player-acts (Act). The relationship-between-scripted-narrative-and-alterbiography subsection effectively dramatizes the Act/Purpose ratio. Burke is wholly absent from Calleja's text (cite_check: 0 hits) — projection only.
expected_uexkull_anchor_candidate: Bedeutungsträger (meaning-carrier) sequence (anticipatory projection per plan §4.1 — provenance: anticipatory-projection). Calleja's alterbiography concept — the player's stringing-together of causally-related segments of synthesis (interaction + interpretation + mental imagery) into an ongoing story — structurally parallels Uexküll's sequence of Bedeutungsträger (meaning-carriers) within an Umwelt: each game-element (NPC, quest item, audio diary, environmental detail) functions as a meaning-bearer whose successive engagement constitutes the player's lived-narrative. The push/pull narrative distinction (Levine on Bioshock) maps especially well — pulled meaning-carriers are biosemiotically active Bedeutungsträger; pushed cut scenes are designer-imposed non-Bedeutungsträger interruptions. Plan-level mapping per §3D.i Section A: 'Narrative -> Bedeutungsträger sequence'. Calleja has zero Uexküll vocabulary; projection only.
expected_ontological_grounding_candidate: muthos / emplotment via Aristotle Poetics (anticipatory projection — provenance: anticipatory-projection). The chapter's central concept — alterbiography as the player's emergent emplotment of game-events into a coherent ongoing story — is the canonical bridge to Aristotelian muthos (Poetics ch.6-10: muthos as synthesis of incidents into a unified action). Calleja's Synthesis subsection (page 128-130) explicitly thematizes the interpretive combination of rules + representation + imagination into a coherent narrative whole — this IS emplotment in everything but name. Secondary anchor: Heidegger BCAP on time-phenomenology / kairotic event-structuring (parallels the macro-phase off-line anticipation of scripted-narrative continuation and the micro-phase moment-by-moment alterbiography generation). Plan-level mapping: 'Narrative -> muthos/emplotment (Aristotle Poetics + Ricoeur Time and Narrative tradition)'. Calleja cites zero Aristotle and only one Heidegger (Question Concerning Technology, p.21); projection only.
